newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open up in becalmed market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open up in becalmed market.

text.p: Singapore shares retained their upward resilience on Thursday but dealers said they expected to see little buying action in a becalmed pre-holiday market.
"Is the market open today?" one dealer quipped.
At 0215 GMT the benchmark Singapore Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was up 8.96 points at 2,204.74 on slim volumes of 23.8 million shares.

Dealers would not normally expect firm upward movement on low volumes, but a 19-point push on 82 million shares on Wednesday confirmed one dealer's view that "prices can do anything at this time of year -- there are no fundamentals."

Motor retailer Cycle & Carriage Ltd surged Singapore $0.20 to S$16.90 at 0240 GMT. Dealers attributed this to a recent government announcement that Singapore would allow more new cars on the road under its Cerfiticate of Entitlement scheme.

Other notable gainers in early trade were DBS Bank foreign, up S$0.20 and Osprey Maritime, up US$0.12, while early losers were Creative Technology, down S$0.50, and OUB foreign and Keppel Corp, both down S$0.10.
Market wide, gainers were ahead of losers 123 to 46 at 0240 GMT.
